name: Club
description: A stout length of hardwood, as blunt as the argument it settles.

name: Dagger
description: A slim double-edged blade that hides in a boot as easily as it finds a rib.

name: Greatclub
description: A tree limb dressed with iron studs, swung in both hands like a felling axe.

name: Handaxe
description: A one-handed axe balanced well enough to split kindling or skulls at a throw.

name: Javelin
description: A light throwing spear made to arc over shields and drop into the line behind.

name: Light Hammer
description: A compact hammer with a spiked poll, handy at the belt and true in flight.

name: Mace
description: A flanged iron head on a short haft, built to ruin whatever armor is in the way.

name: Quarterstaff
description: Six feet of seasoned oak, the honest traveler's weapon and walking stick both.

name: Sickle
description: A crescent harvesting blade that reaps more than wheat when times turn ugly.

name: Spear
description: A leaf-bladed pole arm, cheap to make and the first weapon most militias learn.

name: Light Crossbow
description: A stirrup-cocked crossbow that lets anyone put a bolt through mail with a squeeze.

name: Dart
description: A weighted throwing spike, small enough to palm and quick enough to sting.

name: Shortbow
description: A hunter's bow of modest draw, favored for speed in close woods and saddles.

name: Sling
description: A leather cord and pouch that turns any smooth stone into a shepherd's answer.

name: Battleaxe
description: A broad-bearded war axe equally at home in one hand or gripped with two.

name: Flail
description: A spiked ball on a chain that whips around shields and past careful guards.

name: Glaive
description: A single-edged blade on a long pole, sweeping death at the reach of two men.

name: Greataxe
description: A massive crescent of steel that trades all subtlety for sheer ruin.

name: Greatsword
description: A two-handed blade taller than a child, carried where the fighting is worst.

name: Halberd
description: Axe, hook, and spike married atop a pole — the gate guard's whole argument.

name: Lance
description: A long cavalry spear that turns a charging mount into a thunderbolt.

properties.special: disadvantage within 5 feet; two hands when unmounted

name: Longsword
description: The knight's cruciform blade, quick in one hand and heavier with both.

name: Maul
description: A two-handed sledge that treats plate armor like a stubborn fence post.

name: Morningstar
description: A spiked iron head on a haft, greeting the dawn and the enemy alike.

name: Pike
description: An absurdly long spear that keeps cavalry honest and formations bristling.

name: Rapier
description: A slender thrusting sword for duelists who prefer precision over weight.

name: Scimitar
description: A curved slashing blade that sings in fast, flowing arcs.

name: Shortsword
description: A soldier's stabbing sword, short enough to work where lines press close.

name: Trident
description: A three-tined fishing spear pressed into war, thrown or braced in both hands.

name: War Pick
description: A miner's pick refined for battle, made to punch clean through helm and mail.

name: Warhammer
description: A balanced war hammer with a beaked poll, dreadful in one hand or two.

name: Whip
description: A braided leather lash that stings at a distance polite blades cannot reach.

name: Blowgun
description: A hollow reed that spits needles — quiet, subtle, and rarely fair.

name: Hand Crossbow
description: A pistol-gripped crossbow small enough to fire from beneath a cloak.

name: Heavy Crossbow
description: A windlass-drawn monster of a crossbow that hits like a battering ram.

name: Longbow
description: A man-tall war bow whose draw takes years to earn and seconds to fear.

name: Net
description: A weighted throwing net that tangles rather than wounds, ending fights without blood.

properties.special: restrains the target instead of dealing real harm

name: Padded Armor
description: Layers of quilted cloth that muffle blows and announce your every rustling step.

name: Leather Armor
description: Oil-hardened leather, the quiet standby of scouts and second-story workers.

name: Studded Leather
description: Supple leather reinforced with close-set rivets, protection without the noise.

name: Hide Armor
description: Thick pelts and cured hides, the armor of trappers and those far from smiths.

name: Chain Shirt
description: A shirt of interlocked rings worn under clothing, guarding the torso discreetly.

name: Scale Mail
description: Overlapping metal scales sewn to a leather coat, rattling like angry coins.

name: Breastplate
description: A fitted metal chest piece that guards the vitals and leaves the limbs free.

name: Half Plate
description: Shaped plates over the body's upper half, dashing to look at and loud to wear.

name: Ring Mail
description: Heavy leather sewn with iron rings, a poor cousin to true mail but better than none.

name: Chain Mail
description: A full suit of riveted rings over padding, the working knight's iron skin.

name: Splint Armor
description: Vertical steel strips riveted to a backing, armor that creaks like a drawbridge.

name: Plate Armor
description: Interlocking shaped plates over the whole body, a fortress you wear to war.

name: Shield
description: A wood-and-steel shield strapped to one arm; its ac value of 2 is a +2 bonus added on top of worn armor, not a base.

name: Arrow
description: A goose-fletched arrow, sold by the quiver and spent by the fistful.

name: Crossbow Bolt
description: A short, heavy quarrel that flies flat and hits like a hammer stroke.

name: Sling Bullet
description: A cast lead pellet, meaner in flight than any stone from the riverbed.

name: Blowgun Needle
description: A slender steel needle, more insult than injury until something is smeared on it.

name: Potion of Healing
description: A vial of red liquid that swirls with its own light and knits flesh when drunk.

name: Potion of Greater Healing
description: A treasure-grade draught, deeper crimson than its lesser kin, that closes even grievous wounds.

name: Antitoxin
description: A bitter draught that steels the blood against poison for a time.

name: Holy Water (flask)
description: Blessed water in a stoppered flask, scalding to the undead and the fiendish.

name: Rations (1 day)
description: A day of dried meat, hardtack, and fruit that keeps a body walking.

name: Oil (flask)
description: A pint of lamp oil that feeds a lantern for six hours or a fire for one bad moment.

name: Torch
description: A pitch-soaked brand that burns for an hour and asks nothing but air.

name: Candle
description: A tallow candle shedding a small, honest light for a small, honest hour.

name: Backpack
description: A sturdy leather pack that carries a life on two shoulder straps.

name: Bedroll
description: A rolled sleeping pad that makes any patch of ground almost a bed.

name: Blanket
description: A thick wool blanket, worth more than gold on the wrong night.

name: Rope, Hempen (50 ft)
description: Fifty feet of coarse hemp rope, the most reused tool in any pack.

name: Rope, Silk (50 ft)
description: Fifty feet of silk rope, lighter and kinder to the hands than hemp.

name: Waterskin
description: A leather skin holding four pints of whatever you dare fill it with.

name: Tinderbox
description: Flint, steel, and char cloth in a tin — fire on demand, weather permitting.

name: Healer's Kit
description: Bandages, splints, and salves enough to stabilize the dying ten times over.

name: Lantern, Hooded
description: An oil lantern with a shutter, giving light you can hide at a moment's notice.

name: Lantern, Bullseye
description: A lensed lantern that throws a long cone of light into the dark ahead.

name: Grappling Hook
description: A four-pronged iron hook made to bite stone ledges and hold a climber's faith.

name: Crowbar
description: An iron pry bar that gives leverage to anyone impatient with locks and lids.

name: Hammer
description: A plain work hammer for pitons, tent stakes, and stuck doors.

name: Piton
description: An iron spike hammered into rock so the rope has something to trust.

name: Chalk (1 piece)
description: A stick of chalk for marking turns taken and doors best not reopened.

name: Sack
description: A burlap sack that carries loot out and suspicion in.

name: Pouch
description: A small belt pouch for coins, keys, and other things worth losing quietly.

name: Vial
description: A stoppered glass vial holding four ounces of promise or poison.

name: Flask
description: A pint flask of fired clay, equally suited to spirits and lamp oil.

name: Mirror, Steel
description: A polished steel mirror for grooming, signaling, and peeking around corners.

name: Manacles
description: Iron cuffs and chain, made to keep hands exactly where they were left.

name: Lock
description: A sturdy iron lock with its key, honest work for a thief to undo.

name: Caltrops (bag of 20)
description: A bag of four-pointed spikes that always land tine-up and grudge-first.

name: Ball Bearings (bag of 1,000)
description: A thousand tiny steel spheres, the pratfall waiting inside a pouch.

name: Bell
description: A small brass bell, a tripwire's favorite conversation partner.

name: Chain (10 ft)
description: Ten feet of iron chain for binding gates, beasts, or bargains.

name: Pole (10 ft)
description: Ten feet of pole for prodding floors you would rather not step on.

name: Shovel
description: A digging shovel for camps, latrines, and things better buried.

name: Whetstone
description: A coarse stone that keeps an edge as sharp as its owner's habits.

name: Signal Whistle
description: A shrill tin whistle that carries farther than any shout.

name: Fishing Tackle
description: Line, hooks, and lures — dinner for the patient, practice for the rest.

name: Hunting Trap
description: A saw-toothed leg trap that closes on whatever steps in and apologizes to nothing.

name: Tent, Two-Person
description: A canvas tent that sleeps two friends or one person and their doubts.

name: Climber's Kit
description: Pitons, gloves, harness, and anchors for treating cliffs as staircases.

name: Mess Kit
description: A tin box that unfolds into cup, plate, and pan for the traveling table.

name: Soap
description: A cake of lye soap, the cheapest disguise an adventurer ever wears.

name: Perfume (vial)
description: A vial of scent that opens doors polished boots cannot.

name: Ink (1 oz bottle)
description: An ounce of black ink, enough to write a great many small promises.

name: Ink Pen
description: A cut quill pen that turns ink into contracts, maps, and forgeries.

name: Parchment (one sheet)
description: A single scraped sheet, patient under any hand that can write.

name: Spellbook
description: A blank leather-bound tome of a hundred pages, hungry for careful notation.

name: Holy Symbol (amulet)
description: A consecrated amulet through which the faithful focus their conviction.

name: Thieves' Tools
description: Picks, files, and a small mirror — the polite way through a locked door.

name: Herbalism Kit
description: Clippers, pouches, and a mortar for turning hedgerows into remedies.

name: Disguise Kit
description: Paints, powders, and props for becoming someone the guards are not looking for.

name: Lute
description: A pear-bodied lute strung for ballads, taverns, and the odd desperate distraction.

name: Lyre
description: A small hand-harp of horn and gut string, older music for older rooms.

name: Flute
description: A simple wooden flute, easy to carry and just easy enough to learn to be dangerous.

name: Drum
description: A skin-headed hand drum that carries a march, a warning, or a heartbeat across a camp.

name: Fiddle
description: A working fiddle, more scarred than polished, built for reels rather than recitals.

name: Reed Pipes
description: A bundle of reed pipes bound with twine, thin and piercing over a noisy room.

name: Horn
description: A curved hunting horn that doubles as an instrument when the tune matters more than the signal.

name: Clothes, Common
description: Plain workaday clothes that make you exactly nobody in a crowd.

name: Clothes, Traveler's
description: Hard-wearing boots, cloak, and layers made for the long road.

name: Clothes, Fine
description: Tailored finery that gets you past doormen and into trouble of a richer kind.

name: Iron Pot
description: A heavy cook pot that has ended more hunger than most swords have battles.

name: Magnifying Glass
description: A ground lens that makes small clues large and dry tinder briefly famous.

name: Spyglass
description: A collapsing brass telescope that brings distant trouble close enough to plan for.

name: Portable Ram
description: A short iron-capped ram with handles, for doors that mistake themselves for walls.

name: Hourglass
description: A glass of measured sand for when 'soon' is not a good enough answer.

name: Merchant's Scale
description: A balance scale with weights, keeping every deal honest to the ounce.

name: Book
description: A bound volume on some scholarly matter, worth more to the right reader.

name: Quiver
description: A leather quiver that keeps a score of arrows at your hip and out of the mud.

name: Banded Agate
description: A striped semiprecious stone, small wealth that fits in a boot heel.

name: Garnet
description: A deep red gemstone that catches lamplight like a held breath.

name: Silver Ring
description: A plain silver band, easily pocketed and easily missed.

name: Robe
description: A long flowing garment that falls head to ankle in a single sweep of cloth.

name: Gown
description: A formal full-length garment cut to drape the whole figure.

name: Dress
description: A single-piece garment covering torso and legs together.

name: Cloak
description: A heavy outer wrap that hangs from the shoulders against wind and rain.

name: Coat
description: A long outer layer buttoned against the cold.

name: Jacket
description: A short outer layer for the shoulders and arms.

name: Tunic
description: A plain pull-over top reaching the hip.

name: Shirt
description: A simple cloth top for the upper body.

name: Blouse
description: A soft cut top gathered at the wrist.

name: Vest
description: A sleeveless top layer worn close over the chest.

name: Corset
description: A laced underlayer cinched about the ribs.

name: Chemise
description: A light underlayer worn against the skin beneath other layers.

name: Trousers
description: Sturdy leg coverings for daily wear.

name: Breeches
description: Snug leg coverings ending at the knee.

name: Skirt
description: A garment hanging loose from the waist over the legs.

name: Underwear
description: Plain undergarments worn closest to the skin.

name: Loincloth
description: A simple cloth wrap for the hips.

name: Boots
description: Tall leather footwear laced up the shin.

name: Shoes
description: Simple leather footwear for town cobbles.

name: Sandals
description: Open footwear strapped over the foot.

name: Gloves
description: Fitted coverings for the hands and fingers.

name: Hat
description: A brimmed covering for the head.

name: Wide-Brimmed Mage Hat
description: A tall pointed hat with a drooping brim, the mark of a hedge-spellcaster.

name: Hood
description: A soft cloth head covering that shadows the face.

name: Cap
description: A close-fitting soft covering for the crown of the head.

name: Scarf
description: A length of cloth wound about the neck.

name: Veil
description: A sheer covering draped across the face.
